package_info.package_name: Coinbase.Core (and related: BinanceOfficial, Anarchy.Wrapper.Net, DiscordRichPresence.API, Avalon-Net-Core, Manage.Carasel.Net, Asip.Net.Core, Sys.Forms.26, Azetap.API, AvalonNetCore, Json.Manager.Core, Managed.Windows.Core, Nexzor.Graphical.Designer.Core, Azeta.API)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages use typosquatting and impersonation to appear legitimate, and contain or depend on a malicious init.ps1 script that executes arbitrary PowerShell code on install, downloading and executing a second-stage payload (Impala Stealer) capable of credential and crypto wallet theft. The attack leverages NuGet's autorun script mechanism to achieve code execution without user interaction.

execution_context.trigger: install-time and solution open (via Visual Studio Package Manager Console)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time (and on solution open), the script sets PowerShell execution policy to Unrestricted, downloads an executable from a remote server over HTTP, saves it to the user's AppData directory, and executes it, enabling arbitrary code execution and remote payload delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This script disables PowerShell execution restrictions, downloads and runs an untrusted binary from the internet, and does so automatically on package install or solution open, without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal NuGet packages should not execute code on install, modify execution policies, or download and run external binaries. Legitimate init.ps1 scripts are rare and should not perform these actions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, enterprise packages may use init.ps1 for environment setup, but never for downloading and executing remote binaries.
key_indicators: Sets PowerShell execution policy to Unrestricted
Downloads executable from hardcoded external IP
Runs on install and every solution open
No user interaction or consent required

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Same as above (init.ps1 in dependency package, e.g., Manage.Carasel.Net)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the main package (e.g., DiscordRichPresence.API) pulls in a dependency that contains the malicious init.ps1, which then executes the same download-and-execute behavior as above.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malicious code is hidden in a dependency, making detection harder and increasing the attack surface.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate dependencies should not contain autorun scripts that execute arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Chained dependencies are common, but not for code execution.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Binary payload (Impala Stealer):
- Steals crypto wallets (e.g., Exodus Lightning wallet)
- Exfiltrates data via Discord webhooks
- Extracts and executes code from Electron archives
- Drops updater to C:\Users\user\AppData\Local\Squirrel-2021\Updater.exe
- Connects to C2 for updates
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the downloaded binary searches for crypto wallet data, exfiltrates it via Discord webhooks, extracts code from Electron archives, and installs a persistent updater that checks for new malware versions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The binary performs credential and wallet theft, uses Discord webhooks for exfiltration, and establishes persistence via an updater.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should install or run such a binary as part of its installation process.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; these are classic stealer and persistence behaviors.
key_indicators: References to crypto wallets and Discord webhooks

attack_chain.action: User installs a malicious NuGet package (or a package with a malicious dependency).
init.ps1 script executes automatically, sets PowerShell execution policy to Unrestricted.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of second-stage payload

attack_chain.action: init.ps1 downloads Impala.exe from remote server and executes it.
attack_chain.leads_to: Second-stage payload runs on victim machine

attack_chain.action: Impala.exe (second-stage payload) steals credentials, crypto wallets, exfiltrates data, and establishes persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive data and maintains control

behavioral_signatures: Presence of init.ps1, install.ps1, or uninstall.ps1 in NuGet package tools directory
init.ps1 scripts that set PowerShell execution policy to Unrestricted
init.ps1 scripts that download and execute binaries from external sources
Automatic execution of PowerShell scripts on install or solution open
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan NuGet packages for the presence of init.ps1, install.ps1, or uninstall.ps1 scripts in the tools directory. Flag any scripts that set PowerShell execution policy to Unrestricted, download files from external sources, or execute downloaded binaries. Monitor for network connections to known C2 IPs and Discord webhooks. Watch for creation or execution of suspicious binaries in %APPDATA% or Squirrel-2021 directories. Use package metadata analysis to detect typosquatting and impersonation attempts.
